# conference-mds-resume-r4: handback (Claude Opus 5.5)

**Candidate count: 0.** There is one candidate, MathDB 324342. It is pending independent fidelity review, novelty/significance review, a paper, and root acceptance. No shared counts were edited and nothing was published.

## Result: MathDB 324342 is refuted at p = 19 (full literal Lean endpoint)

**Statement refuted.** Etzion–Vardy–Yaakobi conjecture: for every prime p, the code over F_p generated by any conference matrix of order p+1 is MDS, with dimension (p+1)/2 and distance (p+3)/2.

- It appears as Conjecture 5 in arXiv v1 and v2, and as Conjecture 1 in ISIT 2013.
- It also appears as Conjecture 1 in the author-posted IEEE TIT 2013 version, which I read in part.
- It stays open in all versions and is listed again as open problem 2.

**Counterexample.** Take the Goethals–Seidel skew conference matrix W of order 20. Its row code over F₁₉ is the same as the mod-19 reduction of the lattice Λ(W). That code is a self-dual [20,10,9] code.

- An MDS code here would need d = 11, so the MDS clause and the distance clause both fail.
- The dimension clause (the source's Theorem 4) holds.
- d = 9 exactly was confirmed by a full scan of all 184,756 ten-column sets. There are 180 projective weight-9 words and 6,180 projective weight-10 words.
- Lean proves d ≤ 9, which is enough to refute the conjecture.

**Paley case.** Paley conference matrices always give doubly extended Reed–Solomon codes, so they are MDS for every p. This explains why the source's Paley-only checks up to n = 23 passed. I treat it as context only (it is routine and not credited).

**Lean endpoint.** File: `lean/ConferenceMDS324342.lean`.

- `ConferenceMDS.conjecture5_false : ¬ Conjecture5`.
- The statement uses the source's weighing/conference matrix definition, the F_p row span, `hammingDist` minimum distance, Singleton-equality MDS, and `finrank`.
- Variants, also refuted:
  - textbook conference-matrix definition;
  - minimum-weight definition of distance;
  - each clause on its own.
- The generic bridge `latticeCode_eq_rowCode` proves that the lattice-reduced code equals the row span.
- Non-vacuity control: Paley p = 3 satisfies every clause under the same definitions.

**Fresh extracted replay** (`replays/final`):

- Strict `warningAsError` compile: rc 0. leanchecker: rc 0. Controls: rc 0.

## Old r3 lane: automatic resumption, and how this lane relates to it

The old r3 worker resumed on its own at about 08:00 UTC and finished at 08:21.

- Of the 42 frozen input bindings, two changed during that window: `fresh-corpus-r3/conference/gen_lean.py` and `fresh-corpus-r3/sources/receipts.json`. The r3 worker made those changes; they are not corruption. Nothing in r4 depends on either file. Snapshots and a before/after check are in `provenance/`.
- r3's final Lean file uses the same core definitions as r4 and embeds identical certificate data, because both come from the same frozen witness. **r4 is a replication of that one certificate plus extra bridges and controls. It is not a second witness and not a second candidate.**
- r3 calls the journal body a "2015 IEEE TIT version". The journal paper is TIT 2013; 2015 is only the date the author's copy was uploaded. Part of that copy was read here.

## Reserved r3 IDs

r4 did an in-depth review of 324342 only. The other 39 IDs in `results.json` are marked `not_reviewed_by_r4`. For reference they carry r3's self-reported depth and disposition: 30 literal-only, 2 primary statement, and 8 with proof bodies. r4 did not re-verify those claims.

Per root's instruction, r4 did not start another route:
- 324570 (r3's partial result sup D < 1, with no attainment proof and no Lean) was not duplicated.
- r3's fractional-power and pseudocyclotomic searches were not continued.

## Flags for root and reviewers

1. **Journal-body gap.** The IEEE TIT 2013 math glyphs could not be recovered from the damaged author PDF. The text and structure match the arXiv version. The publisher body was not accessed.
2. **Unread bodies.** Arasu–Gulliver 2001 (codes from conference matrices, likely the [I|W] construction of length 2n; abstract only) and Grassl–Gulliver 2008 were not read. Neither can be ruled out as subsuming this result.
3. **Significance is uncertain.** This is a single explicit computer-found counterexample to a side conjecture, together with a routine Paley dichotomy. I do not certify that it passes the significance bar.
4. **Bounded checks.**
   - Citing works were checked by title only.
   - The MathDB state is known only up to 04:46 UTC, because the inherited 403 was not retried.
   - openai/math is still at head `4eaee875`, with no hits in CONTENTS, history, README or the path screens.
   - Palomar is uninformative or returned the inherited 403.

## Replay

Run from this directory:

    scripts/replay.sh . <fresh-empty-dir>

This regenerates the data and the Lean file, compiles them, and runs the audit, leanchecker and the controls.

Python checks:

    python3 -I scripts/verify_from_scratch.py data/cex20_certificate.json out.json
    python3 -I scripts/paley_control.py
    python3 -I scripts/low_weight_count.py data/verify_from_scratch.json
    python3 -I scripts/gs_reconstruct.py data/cex_20.json data/cex20_certificate.json

Downloaded files are kept untrusted under `web-untrusted/`. Every fetch is logged with its UTC time, HTTP code and sha256 in `logs/fetch-r1.log` and `registry/head-receipt.log`.

Every request was made once. There was no browser, no subagent, no git operation, no shared-file edit and no upload.
